journeyParagraphs: My obsession with computing began with a fundamental curiosity: why should software feel sterile, sluggish, or clinical? As a BCA (Honours) student (Class of 2023–2027) who fell in love with both computational architecture and typographic design, I've spent the past three years bridging the chasm between expressive visual design and rigorous frontend engineering.

Too much of today's web is weighed down by bloated multi-megabyte client-side runtimes, sluggish layout shifts, and inaccessible abstractions. I champion the Renaissance of the Static Web: building sites with zero-runtime CSS architectures, pre-compiled static generators like Eleventy (11ty), and light sprinkling of reactive behavior via Alpine.js.

My design philosophy is grounded in tangibility. Great web software should evoke the physical tactile delight of high-grade editorial print, the responsive elasticity of mechanical instruments, and the unwavering reliability of architectural structures. Every transition is timed to natural human perception, every color palette is tuned for high-contrast accessibility, and every token is engineered for systemic scale.
